identity.title: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS): IX. Magnetohydrodynamic disk winds traced by SO and SO<SUB>2</SUB> in luminous protostars

paper_type_evidence.quote: We employed IRAM Northern Extended Millimeter Array and archival Atacama Large Millimeter Array observations of IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35, respectively, to study the gas kinematics and physical conditions of the corresponding protostellar winds

question.value: Whether high-resolution millimeter observations of thermal tracers (such as SO and SO2) at 100-1000 au scales confirm the presence of rotating magnetohydrodynamic disk winds previously inferred from water maser kinematics at 10-100 au scales in massive protostars.

evidence.quote: It is fundamental to test the MHD DW interpretation based on water maser VLBI at scales of 10–100 au through interferometric observations of thermal tracers at scales of 100–1000 au.

The goal of this article is to further test the water maser MHD DW predictions focusing on the YSOs IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35, representative of the two characteristic maser kinematic configurations observed in POETS.
G035.02+0.35 (tracking center: RA(J2000) = 18h 54m 00.6485s, Dec(J2000) = +02° 01′ 19.278″) was observed within the project 2016.1.01036.S (P.I.: P. Sanhueza) by ALMA in Cycle 4

analysis_steps.goal: Extract spectra and fit physical parameters of molecular gas

method.value: Extract spectra over the area inside the lowest 1.3 mm continuum contour; identify unblended lines using SLIM; perform LTE synthetic spectrum fitting using AUTOFIT with the Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares algorithm.

evidence.quote: we derived the spectral emission in the direction of the YSO by integrating the signal over the area inside the lowest 1.3 mm continuum contour

Using the SLIM (Spectral Line Identification and Modeling) tool of MADCUBA, we surveyed the spectra to search for molecular species with a relatively large number of unblended and optically thin lines

To derive the physical parameters of molecular gas, we used the tool AUTOFIT of MADCUBA, which compares the observed spectra with the LTE synthetic spectra, taking into account all transitions and the line opacities.

Leaving four parameters free to vary, that is, the column density (Ncol), excitation temperature (Tex), line VLSR (v0), and line width (FWHM), AUTOFIT provides the best nonlinear least-squares fit using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm

findings_qualitative.value: In G035.02+0.35, CH3CN, CH3OH, and SO2 emissions are distributed along the disk major axis tracing Keplerian rotation, while SO extends outside the disk into spurs parallel to the rotation axis.

evidence.quote: In G035.02+0.35, the same molecules are instead distributed along the (sky-projected) major axis of the rotating disk reported previously, and their VLSR gradients consistently trace the disk rotation. The corresponding PV plots present Keplerian profiles. SO is the only molecular species whose emission extends well outside the disk.

findings_qualitative.value: In IRAS 21078+5211, molecular emissions (SO, SO2, CH3CN, CH3OH) are elongated along the jet axis and show a transverse velocity gradient consistent with a rotating magneto-centrifugal wind rather than envelope rotation.

evidence.quote: In IRAS 21078+5211, the emissions of several molecules, particularly SO, SO2, CH3CN, and CH3OH, are distributed along the axis of the previously identified radio jet, and present a local standard of rest (LSR) velocity (VLSR) gradient transversal to the jet axis.
Therefore, we can conclude that the observed VLSR gradient is by far too large to correspond to the rotation of the YSO envelope, and has to be linked instead with the rotation of the wind.

findings_qualitative.value: The lack of molecular wind emission besides SO in G035.02+0.35 rules out ambient entrainment by an X-wind and indicates that wind material stems from a warm, shock-ionized disk atmosphere where molecules other than SO are dissociated.

evidence.quote: In G035.02+0.35 the protostellar wind is traced by SO emission only. That already rules out the possibility that we are observing ambient gas entrained in a fast wide-angle X-wind as there is no reasonable explanation why all the other observed molecular emissions would not be present in the wind.
can be well explained in terms of a radially extended MHD DW, rather than a compact X-wind.

claims.hypothesis: Protostellar outflows in IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35 on scales of 100-1000 au are driven by magneto-centrifugally launched rotating winds.
claims.experiment: Analyze ALMA and NOEMA 1.3 mm molecular line kinematics (PV cuts along the disk midplane and off the midplane) and compare velocity gradients across the jet/disk axes.
claims.result: Both sources show Keplerian-like rotation profiles in SO PV diagrams and transverse velocity gradients consistent with wind rotation; envelope rotation would require an unphysically high mass (~44 M_sun vs 5.6 M_sun in IRAS 21078+5211).
claims.finding: The kinematics of SO and SO2 are consistent with a rotating magneto-centrifugal wind launched from the disk.

evidence.quote: Our analysis shows that, in both YSOs, the spatial and velocity distributions of SO are consistent with a rotating wind magneto-centrifugally launched from the YSO disk.
Our analysis of these kinematic findings supports the case of a wind magneto-centrifugally launched from the YSO disk.

claims.hypothesis: The wind launching mechanism corresponds to an extended MHD disk wind rather than an X-wind.
claims.experiment: Compare the radial extensions and column densities of different molecular species (SO, SO2, CH3OH, CH3CN) with shock chemistry models and analyze why molecules other than SO are absent from G035.02+0.35's wind.
claims.result: In IRAS 21078+5211, molecules exhibit a radially nested structure with different excitation and column density behaviors; in G035.02+0.35, only SO extends into the wind while others remain confined to the disk.
claims.finding: Radial chemical stratification and the absence of complex molecules in G035.02+0.35's wind are naturally explained by radially extended MHD DWs emerging from shock-ionized or irradiated disk regions, whereas entrainment by an X-wind is ruled out.

evidence.quote: can be well explained in terms of a radially extended MHD DW, rather than a compact X-wind.
That already excludes the possibility of a X-wind, i.e., that the wind gas is entrained from the surrounding medium, as we should see other molecules, as well.

why_this_data.value: Archival ALMA Cycle 4 Band 6 data and NOEMA long-baseline data overlap in frequency and provide matched linear resolution (~250 au) and velocity resolution (~0.5 km s^-1) for direct comparison of two prototypes from the POETS survey.

evidence.quote: These two interferometric datasets overlap in frequency, and provide comparable linear (≈250 au at the target distance) and velocity (≈0.5 km s−1) resolutions, which is optimal for a comparison of the gas kinematics between the two sources.

why_this_method.value: Briggs weighting (robust = 0.5) balances spatial resolution with sensitivity to extended emission; STATCONT separates continuum from complex line emission statistically; MADCUBA fits multi-transition LTE spectra with opacity corrections.

evidence.quote: with the robust parameter set to 0.5 as a compromise between resolution and sensitivity to extended emission.
STATCONT (cite: Sanc18), a statistical method of estimating the continuum level at each position of the map from the spectral distribution of the intensity at that position.
AUTOFIT of MADCUBA, which compares the observed spectra with the LTE synthetic spectra, taking into account all transitions and the line opacities.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rotation of ambient gas envelope: rejected for IRAS 21078+5211 because the observed transverse velocity gradient would require an unphysical central mass of ~44 M_sun, vastly exceeding the known 5.6 M_sun disk mass.

evidence.quote: We can reasonably rule out that the observed VLSR gradient transversal to the jet axis is due to the rotation of the ambient gas induced by the gravitational force of the YSO.
Therefore, we can conclude that the observed VLSR gradient is by far too large to correspond to the rotation of the YSO envelope, and has to be linked instead with the rotation of the wind.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: X-wind scenario: rejected because ambient material entrained in a wide-angle X-wind would entrain all disk molecules, which contradicts the observation that only SO is found in G035.02+0.35's wind.

evidence.quote: In G035.02+0.35 the protostellar wind is traced by SO emission only. That already rules out the possibility that we are observing ambient gas entrained in a fast wide-angle X-wind as there is no reasonable explanation why all the other observed molecular emissions would not be present in the wind.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photoevaporated disk wind: rejected for G035.02+0.35 because water maser velocities (>20 km s^-1) greatly exceed typical photoevaporation wind speeds (<=10 km s^-1).

evidence.quote: The high maser velocities, ≥20 km s−1, favor a MHD DW rather than a photoevaporated DW, whose typical speeds are ≤10 km s−1 (cite: Hol94; Ale14).

limitations_admitted.value: Single-component LTE assumption in MADCUBA fitting, assuming negligible temperature and density gradients along the line of sight.

evidence.quote: We warn that a single component was fit for each molecular species, under the assumption of negligible density and temperature gradients.

limitations_admitted.value: Insufficient angular resolution to resolve the vertical structure of the disk and separate neutral disk midplane from ionized atmospheric layers.

evidence.quote: Figure 3 shows that the emissions of the molecular lines, dust, and free-free continuum are basically overlapping in the disk. That is certainly due to insufficient angular resolution to resolve the disk structure vertically, since ionized and neutral gas cannot be cospatial.

limitations_admitted.value: SiO 5-4 line is resolved out at the observed high angular resolution.

evidence.quote: For completeness, we note that the SiO 5–4 emission, another potential outflow tracer, is resolved out at these small scales.

referee_caveats_inferred: Assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) for multiple molecular species in shocked wind environments could bias derived excitation temperatures and column densities.
The physical separation between wind and disk kinematics in PV cuts relies on spatial averaging perpendicular to the cut, which might carry minor contamination from disk rotation.
